summary: Baileys fork silently drives installer's WhatsApp session to follow attacker-controlled newsletters and pulls unpinned git dependency
details: This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library that adds covert account-abuse behavior tied to the installer's authenticated WhatsApp session. On every socket connect (validateConnection -> socketConnect in lib/Socket/socket.js), the code reconstructs a URL from a char-code array that resolves to https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skyzopedia/NewsletterID/refs/heads/main/VIP_Push.json, fetches the JSON list, and iterates each entry issuing the WhatsApp w:mex newsletter-follow mutation (query_id 7871414976211147, newsletter_id from the fetched list) against the installer's account. The destination is a third-party GitHub account (skyzopedia) unrelated to the declared publisher (rixxcode/RixxCode) and is attacker-mutable, so whoever controls that repo decides at any time which channels the installer's account subscribes to. A second helper (generateMessageV) XOR(0x17)+base64-decodes an obfuscated string to a hardcoded @newsletter JID and, on a 40s timer, invokes the same newsletter-follow query_id 7871414976211147 - additional covert scaffolding around the same abuse. Additionally, the runtime dependency @rixxcodex/libsignal is declared as github:RixxCode/libsignal with no tag or commit SHA; npm install resolves whatever HEAD of that repo currently returns and executes any lifecycle scripts it contains, giving the repo owner ongoing code-execution control over installers on each fresh install. The base64/XOR obfuscation of both the URL and the JID has no legitimate purpose in a WhatsApp client library and indicates deliberate anti-analysis.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
